knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper aims to classify image noise types and denoising algorithms to improve image quality while preserving structural features. It distinguishes between additive and multiplicative noise and categorizes denoising methods into spatial and transform domain filtering. The study concludes with a comparative performance evaluation and future research directions.

attributes.sources: electronic and photometric sources, noisy channels, measurement errors, quantization errors

attributes.definition: removal or reduction of degradations occurring during image acquisition

attributes.causes: imperfect image formation, relative motion, out-of-focus optical systems, atmospheric turbulence, optical aberrations

attributes.mechanism: low pass filtering on pixel groups

attributes.affiliation: Laxmipati Group of Institutions, RGTU, Bhopal

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text defines digital image representation and classifies common image types by bit depth and color composition. It introduces Gaussian and Salt-and-Pepper noise, describing their statistical properties and causes.

attributes.pixel_value_meaning: brightness of the image at location (x, y)

attributes.values: two discrete values: black (0) and white (1)
attributes.origin: generally created from a gray-scale image
attributes.application: computer vision areas requiring general shape or outline information

attributes.example_bit_depth: 8 bits/pixel allows up to 256 (0-255) brightness levels
attributes.value_mapping: 0 represents black, 255 denotes white, 1-254 represent gray levels

attributes.band_function: each band provides brightness information of the corresponding spectral band

attributes.nature: additive (sum of true pixel value and random Gaussian distributed noise value)

attributes.possible_values: two possible values a and b

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text details the characteristics and causes of salt and pepper, speckle, and Brownian noise in digital images. It describes the probability distributions and typical pixel values associated with these noise types. The section concludes by introducing the classification of denoising algorithms into spatial and transform domain methods.

attributes.causes: malfunctioning of pixel elements in camera sensors, faulty memory locations, timing errors in digitization

attributes.mechanism: low pass filtering on groups of pixels
attributes.assumption: noise occupies higher region of frequency spectrum

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes the development of nonlinear median filters to address the blurring drawbacks of linear filters. It details the properties of mean and Wiener filters, noting their limitations with signal-dependent noise and edge preservation. The passage also introduces wavelet-based denoising methods, distinguishing between linear and nonlinear thresholding approaches.

attributes.examples: weighted median, rank conditioned rank selection, relaxed median
attributes.purpose: overcome the drawback of blurring in linear filters

attributes.optimality: optimal linear filter for Gaussian noise in the sense of mean square error

relationships.target: sharp edges, lines, and fine image details

attributes.requirements: information about spectra of noise and original signal
attributes.implementation: spatial smoothing with model complexity control via window size

attributes.technique: use of low pass filters using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
attributes.mechanism: designing a frequency domain filter and adapting a cut-off frequency
attributes.limitations: time consuming, depends on cut-off frequency and filter function behavior, may produce artificial frequencies

relationships.target: de-correlating noise components from useful signal in frequency domain

attributes.example: Wiener filter in the wavelet domain
attributes.optimal_condition: signal corruption modeled as Gaussian process and accuracy criterion is mean square error (MSE)
attributes.drawback: filtered image may be more visually displeasing than original noisy signal despite reduced MSE

relationships.target: signal corruption is Gaussian and criterion is MSE

entities.name: wavelet-domain spatially adaptive FIR Wiener filtering
aliases: wavelet-domain spatially adaptive FIR Wiener filtering

attributes.constraint: wiener filtering performed only within each scale, intrascale filtering not allowed

attributes.basis: wavelet transform property mapping white noise in signal domain to white noise in transform domain
attributes.principle: signal energy concentrates in fewer coefficients while noise energy does not

attributes.procedure: small coefficients are removed while others are left untouched

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes wavelet-based image denoising techniques, contrasting hard and soft thresholding methods. It details specific adaptive and non-adaptive thresholding algorithms such as VISU Shrink, SURE Shrink, and Bayes Shrink. Additionally, it discusses non-orthogonal wavelet transforms like UDWT and multiwavelets, noting their trade-offs between visual quality and computational complexity.

attributes.drawback: generates spurious blips or artifacts from unsuccessful removal of moderately large noise coefficients

attributes.mechanism: shrinks coefficients above the threshold by the absolute value of the threshold itself

attributes.dependency: depends only on number of data points
attributes.performance: asymptotic equivalence suggesting best performance in terms of MSE when number of pixels reaches infinity
attributes.drawback: yields overly smoothed images due to unwarrantedly large threshold choice

attributes.mechanism: uses a hybrid of the universal threshold and the SURE (Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimator) threshold
minimizes the Bayes' Risk Estimator function assuming generalized Gaussian prior
replaces wavelet coefficient with the weighted average of neighborhood coefficients to minimize generalized cross validation (GCV) function

attributes.benefit: avoids visual artifacts such as pseudo-Gibbs phenomenon
attributes.drawback: adds a large overhead of computations making it less feasible

relationships.target: decomposing the signal to provide visually better solution

attributes.definition: obtained by applying more than one function (scaling function) to given dataset
attributes.impact: enhances performance but further increases computation complexity

knowledge_units.context_summary: Multiwavelets offer superior denoising performance for the Lena image due to properties like short support and higher order vanishing moments. Wavelet coefficient modeling can be deterministic, using tree structures to distinguish signal from noise, or statistical, exploiting multi-scale correlations. The study compares various denoising filters on a 90% noisy Lena image using PSNR and IEF metrics.

attributes.properties: short support, symmetry, higher order of vanishing moments

attributes.focus: exploiting multi resolution properties of Wavelet Transform
attributes.mechanism: identifies close correlation of signal at different resolutions

attributes.tree_representation: levels represent scales, nodes represent coefficients
attributes.signal_characteristic: large coefficients persist along tree branches
attributes.noise_characteristic: lack consistent presence across parent nodes

attributes.focus: multi scale correlation and local neighborhood correlation
attributes.goal: perfect exact modeling of image data
